Examples from the LoCoMo dataset
The LoCoMo dataset consists of very long, multi-turn conversations. Below are examples demonstrating how Memora delivers better memory management compared to state-of-the-art approaches like Mem0 and baseline methods such as RAG. Memora’s design enables more accurate retrieval of memory and context preservation, ensuring better performance on long-term conversational tasks.
Original context in LoCoMo contains conversations that spanned over 20 sessions across more than a year, covering a wide range of events, reflections, and thoughts from the speakers’ life. Original data can be found here: LoCoMo data
Memora performs better in managing memory for long context because its index–value representation not only enables pinpoint retrieval but also preserves the richness of the original context. The index acts as a guide to navigate memory, while the memory items themselves are stored with the right level of detail, maintaining relationships and meaning. In some cases, this indexing also allows Memora to link related information across different parts of the context, creating a more coherent and connected view that supports reasoning. In contrast, Mem0 stores very small factual fragments without capturing their connections. Even when a memory exists, it can easily get lost during retrieval. Sometimes, the memory isn’t even created at all. RAG faces a different limitation: it chunks the original context into large blocks, which makes retrieval coarse-grained. Each chunk contains too much information, so the relevant detail is buried among unrelated content, making it hard to pinpoint and retrieve the context that matters.
